blocks.text: Why do property managers ask for bank statements

Asking for bank statements is a defensive measure. It allows you to see if the income claimed on an application matches the actual deposits. It also reveals recurring payments that might indicate hidden debt or financial instability.
The operational cost of manual screening

Manual screening is slow and prone to human error. When you review documents one by one in Preview on your Mac, you lose time that could be spent on property maintenance or owner relations. The cost of missing a fraudulent application is high. Eviction costs can reach $25,000, and nearly a quarter of these cases involve applicants who submitted fake documents.
Why fraud is rising in rental applications

Fraudulent actors use sophisticated tools to create fake pay stubs and bank statements. If your systems do not communicate with each other, these documents often pass inspection. The lack of an integrated verification process creates a gap that professional scammers exploit daily.
How to fix your screening workflow

items: Create written, standardized criteria for every applicant to ensure Fair Housing compliance.
Use integrated platforms like AppFolio or DoorLoop to centralize document collection.
Implement AI-based verification tools that check documents against known fraud patterns.
Audit your screening process periodically to remove manual bottlenecks.

blocks.text: Always follow your company or brokerage rules regarding client data privacy and document storage. Keep sensitive financial information encrypted and restricted to authorized personnel only.
blocks.title: Data Privacy Reminder

blocks.text: Using your Mac to manage the process

Your Mac is a powerful tool for managing these tasks. Most property management software runs in your browser, such as Safari or Chrome. You can use Keychain to manage passwords for different portals. Use Preview to quickly redact sensitive account numbers on PDFs before storing them.

items: Applying different standards to different applicants, which can lead to discrimination lawsuits.
Accepting screenshots of bank statements instead of official PDF exports.
Failing to verify the identity of the applicant alongside their financial documents.
Relying on manual entry instead of automated integrations for background checks.

faq.question: Can I legally require bank statements?
faq.answer: Yes, in most jurisdictions, you can require documentation to verify income and financial stability, provided you apply the same requirements to all applicants.

faq.question: What should I look for in a bank statement?
faq.answer: Look for consistent deposits that match the applicant's stated income, and watch for signs of overdrafts or suspicious recurring transfers.

faq.question: How do I spot a fake bank statement?
faq.answer: Look for inconsistencies in font, alignment, or math. Modern fraud detection software can often flag these automatically.
